content.text:
I've built the course registration app in `/work` using plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no dependencies. To use it, open `index.html` in a browser, or run `python3 -m http.server` in `/work` and visit `localhost:8000`.

**Files**
```
index.html      Home
catalog.html    Course catalog
register.html   Registration
profile.html    Student profile
css/styles.css  All styling, including the responsive layouts
js/data.js      17 sample courses across 7 departments
js/app.js       Shared parts (navigation bar, modal, pop-up messages, storage) plus the logic for each page
```

**What's on each page**
- **Navigation bar** on every page. It highlights the current page, shows a count of your registered courses, and turns into a menu button on phones.
- **Home:** a large colourful banner with a search box (it takes you to the catalog with results), stat cards, tiles for each department that open the catalog filtered to that department, three featured courses, and a short "how registration works" section.
- **Catalog:** search as you type (by code, title, instructor or keyword) and five dropdowns: department, level, credits, meeting day and sort order. There's also an "open seats only" switch, labels showing which filters are on, and a reset button. Each course card has its own colour, a bar showing how full it is, and a seats-left label.
- **Registration:** a three-step form: your details (checked as you fill them in), course checkboxes you can search and filter, and a policy agreement. A side panel tracks your credits. Submitting opens a **confirmation modal** listing the courses and your new credit total.
- **Profile:** a card with your initials and details, enrollment stats (including full-time or part-time status), a weekly timetable grid, and an edit form that can be opened and closed.
- **Registered courses table:** appears on both the registration and profile pages, with a total row and a Drop button for each course (which asks you to confirm first).

**Registration rules:** it blocks a course if you're already registered, the course is full, it clashes with another course in your schedule, or you'd go over the 18-credit limit. You get a warning modal saying exactly which rule was broken. Registrations and profile changes are saved in the browser, so they're still there after a reload.

**Responsive design:** layouts are set for desktop, tablet (under 1024px), mobile (under 860px) and small phones (under 600px). On mobile the courses table turns into stacked cards. Animations are turned off for users whose system asks for reduced motion.

I've built the course registration app in `/work` using plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no dependencies. To use it, open `index.html` in a browser, or run `python3 -m http.server` in `/work` and visit `localhost:8000`.

**Files**
```
index.html      Home
catalog.html    Course catalog
register.html   Registration
profile.html    Student profile
css/styles.css  All styling, including the responsive layouts
js/data.js      17 sample courses across 7 departments
js/app.js       Shared parts (navigation bar, modal, pop-up messages, storage) plus the logic for each page
```

**What's on each page**
- **Navigation bar** on every page. It highlights the current page, shows a count of your registered courses, and turns into a menu button on phones.
- **Home:** a large colourful banner with a search box (it takes you to the catalog with results), stat cards, tiles for each department that open the catalog filtered to that department, three featured courses, and a short "how registration works" section.
- **Catalog:** search as you type (by code, title, instructor or keyword) and five dropdowns: department, level, credits, meeting day and sort order. There's also an "open seats only" switch, labels showing which filters are on, and a reset button. Each course card has its own colour, a bar showing how full it is, and a seats-left label.
- **Registration:** a three-step form: your details (checked as you fill them in), course checkboxes you can search and filter, and a policy agreement. A side panel tracks your credits. Submitting opens a **confirmation modal** listing the courses and your new credit total.
- **Profile:** a card with your initials and details, enrollment stats (including full-time or part-time status), a weekly timetable grid, and an edit form that can be opened and closed.
- **Registered courses table:** appears on both the registration and profile pages, with a total row and a Drop button for each course (which asks you to confirm first).

**Registration rules:** it blocks a course if you're already registered, the course is full, it clashes with another course in your schedule, or you'd go over the 18-credit limit. You get a warning modal saying exactly which rule was broken. Registrations and profile changes are saved in the browser, so they're still there after a reload.
